```{r}
source("assets/setup.R")
f <- function(x, d = 2) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = d)
pm <- round(100 * colMeans(is.na(ncd)), 0)
dat2 <- dat |> mutate(smoker = factor(smoker, labels = c("No", "Yes")))
imp <- mice(dat2, m = 20, maxit = 10, seed = 2038, printFlag = FALSE)
m_cc <- lm(sbp ~ age + sex + bmi + smoker + activity, data = dat)
s <- summary(pool(with(imp, lm(sbp ~ age + sex + bmi + smoker + activity))))
cc_b <- coef(m_cc)[["bmi"]]; mi_b <- s$estimate[s$term == "bmi"]
```

::: {.sheet}

## 1 · Three mechanisms

| | Missingness depends on | Complete-case | Multiple imputation |
|---|---|---|---|
| **MCAR** | nothing | unbiased, loses precision | valid |
| **MAR** | **observed** data | can be **biased** | **valid** |
| **MNAR** | the **missing value** itself | biased | **biased** unless an MNAR assumption is modelled |

MAR = "explained by observed variables", **not** "random". **MNAR cannot be tested** from the observed data.

## 2 · Describe it first

`colMeans(is.na(d))` · `sum(complete.cases(d))` · `md.pattern(d)` · `naniar::miss_var_summary()`, `gg_miss_upset()`, `vis_miss()`. Compare observed variables between **complete and incomplete** adults; model `is.na(x) ~ observed variables` (include the **outcome**). `naniar::mcar_test()`: rejecting MCAR does **not** prove MAR.

Our cohort: BMI **`r pm[["bmi"]]`%**, HbA1c **`r pm[["hba1c"]]`%**, activity **`r pm[["activity"]]`%**, smoking **`r pm[["smoker"]]`%**, SBP **`r pm[["sbp"]]`%**; only **`r f(100 * mean(complete.cases(ncd)), 0)`%** of adults complete.

## 3 · Simple methods: do not use

| Method | Problem |
|---|---|
| **Complete case** | loses data; biased if missingness depends on the outcome |
| **Mean imputation** | shrinks variance, biases, wrong SE |
| **Missing indicator** | biased even under MAR |
| **Single imputation** | SE too small (imputed values treated as real) |

BMI slope in the SBP model (truth about 0.80): complete case **`r f(cc_b)`**, multiple imputation **`r f(mi_b)`**.

## 4 · mice in six lines

```r
dat$smoker <- factor(dat$smoker)                      # binary -> logreg
imp <- mice(dat, m = 20, maxit = 10, seed = 1)        # drop the id first
plot(imp); densityplot(imp, ~ bmi)                    # converged? plausible?
fit <- with(imp, lm(sbp ~ age + sex + bmi))
summary(pool(fit), conf.int = TRUE)                   # Rubin's rules
```

Methods: `pmm` (continuous, default), `logreg` (binary factor), `polyreg` (unordered factor), `polr` (ordered). Inspect `imp$method`, `imp$predictorMatrix`, `imp$loggedEvents`.

## 5 · Rubin's rules

::: {.eq}
estimate = mean of the m estimates       T = W + (1 + 1/m) B       W = mean within-imputation variance, B = variance of the estimates
:::

**fmi** (`pool(fit)$pooled`): share of the variance due to the missing data (not the % missing).

## 6 · Doing it well

::: {.good}
- Put the **outcome**, all **analysis variables**, **interactions/curves** you will fit, and **auxiliary** variables in the imputation model
- **m** at least the % of incomplete cases (at least 20); fixed **seed**
- **Derive** variables (e.g. hypertension) **after** imputing: `complete(imp, "long", include = TRUE)` then `as.mids()`
- Test several coefficients with **`D1()`**; do not average p-values
- Check **convergence** and imputed **distributions**
:::

## 7 · MNAR sensitivity (delta adjustment)

```r
post <- make.post(dat); post["hba1c"] <- "imp[[j]][, i] <- imp[[j]][, i] + 0.5"
imp_d <- mice(dat, m = 20, post = post)
```

Run delta = 0 (MAR), 0.2, 0.4 ... and ask **at which delta does the conclusion change** (tipping point). Tails and prevalences are most sensitive: HbA1c mean `r f(mean(dat$hba1c, na.rm = TRUE))` observed.

## 8 · Report

Amount of missing data per variable and complete cases · assumed mechanism and reasons · method (MICE, pmm), **m**, iterations, variables used · pooled estimates and complete-case comparison · MNAR sensitivity analysis.

*Missing values were handled by multiple imputation by chained equations (20 imputations, predictive mean matching, outcome and auxiliary variables included, Rubin's rules); a delta-adjustment analysis explored departures from MAR.*

:::
